A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AcTOL research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulation success rates, ablations, linguistic-perturbation experiments, and learned-reward analyses in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains original simulation and representation analyses and adds physical-robot trials, hyperparameter sensitivity results, and expanded linguistic-perturbation experiments.

M1.justification: The VLO scoring function and negative set, Brownian-bridge loss, CLIP encoders, and frozen-encoder-plus-MLP policy approach are retained. V2 introduces no new AcTOL component; its reported hyperparameter revisions concern experimental settings.

E1.justification: V2 adds three physical Unitree D1 tasks—picking a cup and opening/closing an indexed drawer—and a fifth Metaworld task, drawer opening. It also expands instruction scenarios to lexical substitutions and complex contextual requests. EPIC-KITCHEN-100 pretraining and the original simulation tasks remain.

E2.justification: CLIP, R3M, LIV, and DecisionNCE remain the LCBC and main reward comparators. Linguistic-perturbation comparisons still use LIV and DecisionNCE. The added robot and drawer-opening experiments extend the existing comparator set; newly cited methods such as UVD are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The stated loss weight changes from 100 in v1 to 0.1 in v2, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. V2 adds a physical-robot protocol using 60 demonstrations per task, 50K policy-training steps, and final-checkpoint evaluation. Sensitivity experiments introduce additional configurations; existing simulation checkpoint-selection procedures remain.

E4.justification: V2 adds sensitivity analyses for 3/5/10 sampled frames and loss weights 0.01/0.1/1 in Figure 7. Linguistic robustness expands from two conversational templates to four variants, including lexical substitutions and GPT-4o-generated contextual instructions. The Brownian-bridge ablation, t-SNE comparison, and original reward case studies are retained.

E5.justification: V2 adds numerical ± uncertainty values to the previously mean-only per-task LCBC tables. V1 already reported three simulation seeds, error-bar plots, and uncertainty for linguistic perturbations. V2 additionally specifies ten fixed-seed evaluation trials per physical-robot task; no increase in retained simulation seed counts is established.

E6.justification: V2 adds robot success rates of 50%, 80%, and 90% for AcTOL, drawer-opening results, sensitivity results, and expanded perturbation outcomes. Original per-task LCBC means are retained. Franka relative gains at 15/25 demonstrations are corrected from 46.4%/26.3% to 43.06%/24.40%. V2 Table 1 still reports four-task Metaworld averages while Tables 10–12 aggregate five tasks; these expanded averages are not matched-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V1's VLO definition and Theorems 4.2–4.4 correspond to v2's Definition 1 and Theorems 1–3. Their assumptions, bounds, and appendix derivations retain their mathematical substance. The separate theory section adds explanation and reorganizes existing results.

C1.justification: The central ordering, continuity, and language-robustness contributions remain. The abstract and introduction broaden the claimed empirical validation to physical-robot control and complex linguistic perturbations, while dropping the abstract's numerical 'up to 49%' headline.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the simulation/hardware caveat with substantive limitations concerning repetitive or cyclic actions and human-to-robot distribution gaps. It adds interpretations of cup-handle grasping difficulty and weak sensitivity to the loss weight. V1's extended explanation of R3M's differing performance across environments is removed.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's pretraining and simulation documentation, v2 specifies physical-robot data collection, third-person camera observations, 20 Hz synchronization, Unitree Go teleoperation, GTX 880M deployment, and robot-policy hyperparameters. It also adds simulation compute accounting. The code URL remains unchanged, but the abstract additionally advertises demonstration videos.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including π0, Octo, SpatialVLA, GPT-4o, and UVD, with a brief new argument connecting AcTOL to long-horizon decomposition. LOReL and t-SNE references disappear. The central positioning against goal-reaching vision-language pretraining remains.

P1.justification: Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 6, theory becomes a separate section, trajectory visualization merges into reward analysis, and appendix proofs move behind experimental details. Experimental discussion and the conclusion are substantially revised, and the author block changes.

P2.justification: V2 switches to a single-column layout, redraws the framework diagram, adds an introductory figure, and expands the environment illustration. Simulation bars become Table 1; linguistic results gain a new plot and expanded table. Sensitivity and robot-interface figures are added, while v1's component-comparison table is removed.

improvement.justification: V1 explicitly deferred real-world deployment; v2 supplies comparative physical-robot trials in Table 2, substantially strengthening evidence for its central transfer claim. Broader language tests, sensitivity analysis, and explicit applicability limitations further improve the paper. The robot study remains limited to ten fixed-seed trials per task, and inconsistent Metaworld aggregates weaken reporting reliability, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gain in direct physical validation.
